# nonCellGridRange

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a single-cell range.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonCellGridRange() — Checks whether a value is **not** a single-cell range. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/sheet</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonCellGridRange(gridRange: GridRange): boolean;
```

`nonCellGridRange(value)` is the same test as `!isCellGridRange(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

One row and one column, measured by the bounds rather than by how the range was written: the end indices are exclusive, so a single cell is `endRowIndex - startRowIndex === 1` and the same for the columns. A range with a bound left out is open in that direction and is never a single cell.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter   | Type        | Description              |
| :---------- | :---------- | :----------------------- |
| `gridRange` | `GridRange` | The grid range to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a single-cell range; otherwise `false`.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonCellGridRange({ startRowIndex: 0, endRowIndex: 2, startColumnIndex: 0, endColumnIndex: 1 }); // => true
nonCellGridRange({}); // => true
nonCellGridRange(null); // => true
nonCellGridRange({ startRowIndex: 0, endRowIndex: 1, startColumnIndex: 0, endColumnIndex: 1 }); // => false
```
